Mic check. This is a mic check. This is for the vote on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards, and Ethics. Today is March 26, 2026. Recorded by Walter Lewis in Hearing Room 1.

Good morning, and welcome to today's New York City Council vote for the Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards, and Ethics. At this time, I would like to remind everyone to silence all electronic devices. Also, at this point going forward, no one is to approach the dais. Chair, we're ready to begin.

Good morning, and welcome to this meeting of the Committee on Rules, Privileges, Elections, Standards, and Ethics. I am Council Member Sandra Ung, Chair of the Committee. Before we begin, I would like to recognize the other Members of this Committee who are present (INAUDIBLE) Encarnación, Carr, Riley, Lee, and Abreu. I also like to acknowledge the Counsel to the Committee, Jeff Campagna, and the Committee Staff that worked on the matters before the Committee today, Director of Public Integrity Francesca DellaVecchia; Deputy

COMMITTEE ON RULES, PRIVILEGES, ELECTIONS, STANDARDS AND ETHICS 3 Director of Public Integrity Alycia Vassell; and the Chief Ethics Counsel Pearl Moore. Today, we are voting on two items that the Committee heard on March 12, 2026. We are voting on a Resolution to approve M41, the Mayor's request pursuant to Sections 31 and 2301 of the New York City Charter for the Council's advice and consent in relation to the appointment by the Mayor of Midori Valdivia to serve as a member of the New York City Taxi and Limousine Commissioner for the remainder of a seven-year term that will expire on January 31st, 2031. The Mayor has indicated his intent to designate Ms. Valdivia to serve as the Chair of the TLC. We're also voting a resolution to approve M51, a request by the Comptroller pursuant to Section 2602 of the New York City Charter for the Council advice and consent regarding the appointment of Wayne G. Hawley to serve the Conflict of Interest Board to serve the remainder of the six-year term that will expire on March 31st, 2028. I now call on the Clerk to call the roll.

Matthew DeStefano, Committee Clerk. Committee on Rules,

COMMITTEE ON RULES, PRIVILEGES, ELECTIONS, STANDARDS AND ETHICS 4 Privileges, Elections, Standards and Ethics. Roll call vote. All items are coupled. Chair Ung.
Williams. Banks. Encarnación. COUNCIL MEMBER ENCARNACIÓN: Aye.

Thank you, Chair. Just a couple of words about the two nominees that are before us. With respect to Mr. Wayne Hawley, I'm really grateful to the Comptroller for appointing him to continue to serve on the Conflicts of Interest Board. I think he's somebody

COMMITTEE ON RULES, PRIVILEGES, ELECTIONS, STANDARDS AND ETHICS 5 who over the course of his career as a leading staffer at that institution and then as a Commissioner, he's shown that he has great wisdom and judgment and experience that should be retained for the benefit of the City at COIB, and I'm very happy to be supporting his appointments to a different spot on the Conflicts of Interest Board, but nonetheless, that will allow him to continue to serve. With respect to Midori Valdivia, who's the Mayor's appointee to the Taxi and Limousine Commission, I have a number of good things I could say about her. I know that in her time at TLC, she made sure Staten Island had its first TLC office, which is actually located in my District. And in particular, her championing of public-private partnerships in her time at the Port Authority, which led to real positive changes, in particular the Goethals Bridge replacement project, which I regard as one of the great public works successes in our region. But despite this, you know, her vote as a member of the MTA board to impose congestion pricing on folks coming into most of Manhattan, I think is not something that I can overlook. I think that it's something that has imposed significant costs on my

COMMITTEE ON RULES, PRIVILEGES, ELECTIONS, STANDARDS AND ETHICS 6 constituents in particular, as well as a lot of outer borough and other residents throughout New York City, and it's also being done in the name of financing the MTA's capital plan, which again is not one that reflects borough equity. It is not one that brings investment back to the communities that it's charging. So, I unfortunately will not be able to vote in favor of her appointment today. So, with that being said, I'll be voting no on M41 and aye on the rest.
By a vote of seven in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions, M51 has passed. By a vote of six in the affirmative, one in the negative, and no abstentions, M41 is passed.
I would like to keep the vote open.
Continuation of roll call. Council Member Krishnan.

I vote aye.

Final vote: M51, nine in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions. M41, eight in the affirmative, one negative, and no abstentions.
